summary.headline: Apcotex Q2 FY27 revenue rose 48% YoY to Rs 499 crore, but EBITDA margin eased to 11.69% as gross margins compressed.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 operating revenue was Rs 499 crore (+48% YoY) on 7% volume growth, with operating EBITDA of Rs 58 crore (+44% YoY) and PAT of Rs 35 crore (+38% YoY). EBITDA margin was 11.69% versus 12.06% a year earlier, and PAT margin was 6.98%. H1 FY27 was the company's strongest half-year, with revenue of Rs 1,025 crore (+44%), EBITDA of Rs 175 crore (+121%, margin 17.12%) and PAT of Rs 114 crore (+156%). Management attributed the Q2 margin dip to high raw material prices, about 1.5% inventory losses, and more aggressive pricing to win export volumes.

segments.name: Nitrile latex
segments.commentary: Running close to full capacity; management said Q1 margins were a blip and Q2 normalised but remain much better than the last three years. Further expansion decision deferred pending a couple more quarters of margin data.

segments.name: NBR (solid nitrile butadiene rubber)
segments.commentary: Sole Indian producer, entirely import-dependent; plant has run at full capacity for about 1.5 to 2 years. Capex project targeted for commissioning around April 2027. H1 NBR margin said to be slightly higher than synthetic latex.

segments.name: Synthetic latex (SBR)
segments.commentary: Serves about five industries; construction strongest, paper and textiles decent, tyres okay, carpets a laggard due to MENA dependence. SBR latex plant at Valia expected around Q2 of next year.

guidance_outlook: Management targets a long-run volume CAGR of about 10% (20-30% above GDP growth) over the next three to five years, with construction faster and carpet slower.
Management aims for EBITDA margin closer to 15% but is comfortable with about 12% given high raw material costs; focus is on volumes, EBITDA per ton and ROCE.
Part of the Q1 inventory losses should reverse as prices rose again in October-November due to oil; Q3 is only one month old, so outcome uncertain.
NBR capacity expected to commission around April 2027, with utilisation ramping over two to three years.
Remaining capex outflow of about Rs 155 crore (of Rs 220 crore total, about Rs 65 crore spent) to be spent through next year and beyond; SBR may slip into a later quarter.
capex_capacity: Valia expansion capex of Rs 210 crore (later referenced as Rs 220 crore) largely on track; about Rs 65 crore spent, about Rs 155 crore remaining.
NBR (solid) plant targeted for commissioning around April 2027; SBR latex plant at Valia expected around Q2 of next fiscal year.
Nitrile latex expansion undecided; most engineering ready, requiring only added reactors; board did not decide at its 28 October meeting.
Most plants running at 80-90% utilisation; NBR plant at full capacity; new capacity needed for growth in the next two to three years.
Company does not disclose segment-wise volumes.
demand_pricing: Export volumes recovered in Q2 after a decline in Q1; shipping to Saudi Arabia (West Coast) and Fujairah improved versus Q1, though MENA remains tight.
Management said it was more aggressive on pricing to win orders in other markets, which lowered gross margin; EBITDA per ton was higher YoY.
Competitor shutdowns in Q1 benefited the company, which kept plants running; overcapacity in nitrile latex persists from COVID-era additions.
Carpet volumes hit by US tariffs, the war and high ocean freight; management said Q2 carpet volumes were broadly flat YoY.
Paper overcapacity increasing, though final paper demand is okay; construction is the strongest segment.
India accounts for 65-67% of sales; Q2 seasonally weak due to monsoon-related demand dip.

qa_highlights.question: Why are gross margins at a four-quarter low, and what drove the rise in export volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited high raw material prices, about 1.5% inventory losses in the quarter, and more aggressive pricing. Exports improved with better ship availability to Saudi Arabia and Fujairah, plus orders from other markets. EBITDA per ton and ROCE were better YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the nitrile latex cycle and does oversupply persist?
qa_highlights.answer: Running close to full capacity; Q2 margins normalised from a strong Q1 but are much better than the last three years. Overcapacity from COVID-era additions remains even after some smaller and older plants shut. Expansion decision deferred for a couple more quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a timeline and funding breakup for the Rs 210 crore expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: NBR commissioning targeted for about April 2027, with two to three years to full utilisation. Management said about Rs 65 crore is spent and Rs 155 crore remains, but did not give a debt versus internal accrual split in the answer.

qa_highlights.question: Which synthetic latex industries are growing or lagging?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction (repairs, waterproofing, oil drilling) has grown strongly; paper and textiles are decent and tyres okay. Carpets are the laggard due to MENA and Western market exposure from tariffs, war and freight costs.

qa_highlights.question: What long-term volume growth is expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects about 10% average volume CAGR over three to five years, driven by population and GDP growth in India and Southeast Asia, plus substitution of European supply in MENA.

qa_highlights.question: Is the sequential Q2-to-Q3 decline a pattern, and is there a strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management acknowledged the Q1-to-Q2 seasonal decline from monsoon-linked demand. It said it had not analysed Q2-to-Q3 patterns and would review five years of data. It urged investors to focus on annual trends, given oil-linked inventory gains and losses.

risks_watch: Gross and EBITDA margin volatility from oil-linked raw material prices and inventory gains or losses; Q3 pricing recovery depends on the rest of the quarter.
Carpet segment volume weakness from MENA and Western exposure, freight costs and tariffs.
Nitrile latex overcapacity may cap margins; the expansion decision is pending.
NBR commissioning slip beyond April 2027 would delay ramp-up; SBR plant timing may slip to a later quarter.
Working capital elevated from higher input costs, with inventory and receivables up; the company remains net cash positive as of 30 September 2026.
Anti-dumping on NBR imports was not granted, per management.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes, returns and H1 performance, but defensive on quarter-on-quarter margin trends and on segment-level disclosure. Management was candid that Q2 gross margins fell and that the nitrile latex expansion is on hold.
key_quotes: So, obviously, ideally, we would want it closer to 15 %. But we are quite happy with the 12% given the high cost of raw materials today and the high selling prices as well as a result.
I would say 20-30% over GDP. So, 10-12% a year is what we expect.
So, out of Rs. 220 crores, about Rs. 65 crores we have spent and Rs. 155 crores is to be outflown by next year, till the time of project completion and sometime thereafter.

growth.why: Management targets about 10-12% volume CAGR over 3-5 years (the 10% figure is a multi-year volume guide, used here as the revenue proxy), backed by NBR capacity due around April 2027 and SBR at Valia around Q2 next year, with Rs 155 crore of the Rs 220 crore capex still to spend; most plants run at 80-90% and NBR at full capacity, but nitrile latex expansion is undecided.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin eased to 11.69% from 12.06% on high raw material prices and ~1.5% inventory losses, but management expects part of Q1 losses to reverse as oil-linked prices rose in Oct-Nov and targets about 12% (15% aspirational).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: NBR solid plant (Rs 220 crore Valia capex, about Rs 65 crore spent) is on track for commissioning around April 2027, and SBR latex at Valia is expected around Q2 FY28, though SBR may slip; nitrile latex expansion is deferred.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides about 10% volume CAGR over 3-5 years, Q2 volumes grew 7% YoY, and most plants run at 80-90% utilisation with NBR at full capacity.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation is 80-90% with NBR at full capacity for 1.5-2 years, but the nitrile latex expansion decision was deferred for a couple more quarters after the 28 October board meeting.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management was candid that Q2 gross margins fell to a four-quarter low and that Q3 pricing recovery is uncertain, with only one month of Q3 elapsed.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Carpet volumes are flat YoY and hit by US tariffs, MENA and freight, nitrile latex overcapacity persists, and SBR or NBR timelines could slip.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: NBR solid capacity (Rs 220 crore Valia project) is targeted for about April 2027 and SBR latex at Valia for around Q2 FY28, both new product-capacity launches.

rows.label: Export recovery to MENA and other markets
rows.why: Exports recovered in Q2 after a Q1 decline with better ship availability to Saudi Arabia and Fujairah, and management is winning orders in other markets, though MENA remains tight.

rows.label: Working capital build from higher input costs
rows.why: Inventory and receivables are up on higher input costs, though the company stays net cash positive as of 30 September 2026.

rows.label: Anti-dumping relief on NBR imports
rows.why: Management said anti-dumping on NBR imports was not granted, leaving the sole Indian producer exposed to imports.

tone.note: Management was confident on volumes, ROCE and H1 performance (H1 EBITDA +121%) and on NBR timing, but defensive on Q2 gross margin decline, quarter-on-quarter trends and segment disclosure, with the nitrile latex expansion on hold; analysts pressed on margins, oversupply and the Q2-to-Q3 pattern.
